hints.title: Use the descending term
hints.body: Write the exponents of x in the first four terms in descending order. Match the fourth one to the power given in the question.
hints.recap: Ascending and descending term numbers refer to different powers of x.
hints.pitfall: The first descending term has power n.

recall.reminder: Ascending and descending term numbers refer to different powers of x.

hints.title: Write both coefficients
hints.body: In (a+bx)n, the coefficient of xk is (nk)an−kbk. Use the two stated ascending terms.
hints.recap: Keep the combination factor and the powers of both constants.
hints.pitfall: The constant term is the first term in ascending order.
hints.pause: Write and simplify the two equations for a and b.

recall.reminder: Keep the combination factor and the powers of both constants.

hints.title: Divide the equations
hints.body: The question asks for a ratio, so try dividing one coefficient equation by the other.
hints.recap: Comparing coefficient ratios can find a/b without finding a and b separately.
hints.pitfall: The given nonzero coefficients must justify your division.
hints.pause: Cancel common factors, then square the ratio you need.

recall.reminder: Comparing coefficient ratios can find a/b without finding a and b separately.

solution:
1. Find the degree. The fourth term in descending powers contains xn−3. Since this is x3, we have n=6.

2. Use the ascending coefficients. (62)a4b2=105 and (63)a3b3=210. As the combination factors are 15 and 20, these become a4b2=7 and a3b3=212.

3. Divide and square. Both a and b are nonzero because the given coefficients are nonzero. Dividing gives ab=721/2=23. Therefore (ab)2=49.

Answer B. Dividing the equations avoids solving for a and b individually.
knowledgePattern: Use term positions to identify degree, then divide binomial coefficients
